verifications.claim: Almost all male U.S. citizens and male immigrants living in the U.S. aged 18–25 must register with the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Almost all male US citizens and male immigrants, who are 18 through 25, are required to register with Selective Service." (R1); "male U. S. citizen living in the U.S. ... or a male immigrant ... age 18 through 25" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches phrasing and details in R1.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration is a legal requirement.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "are required to register" (R1); "you are required to register" (R2); "required to register with the Selective Service System" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state it is required by law.

verifications.claim: Automatic Selective Service System registration is launching in 2026 for many.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "automatically register eligible men ... beginning in December ... SSS will implement the change by December 2026" (R3); "automatic registration will be in place by December 2026" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm federal automatic registration by December 2026.

verifications.claim: Male citizens and immigrants including undocumented, refugees, and asylum seekers born in 1960 or later living in the U.S. between 18 and 25 years old must register with the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "This includes U.S. born and naturalized citizens, parolees, undocumented immigrants, legal permanent residents, asylum seekers, refugees" (R1); "men born before 1960 get their Selective Service record" implying post-1960 for current (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Immigrant types and age directly supported; 'born 1960 or later' supported indirectly via record distinctions but not precisely stated for requirement.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration must occur within 30 days of turning 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "30 days after their 18th birthday" (R1); "self-register within 30 days of their 18th birthdays" (R3); "within 30 days of his 18th birthday" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact timing directly stated across sources.

verifications.claim: Late Selective Service System registration is accepted until age 26.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "accepts late registrations until age 26" (R3); "Selective Service accepts late registrations up until a man reaches his 26th birthday" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Directly confirmed in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration can be completed online at SSS.gov.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "You may register online with the Selective Service System" (R2); "Men 18-25 can register online" (R9); register page at sss.gov (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states online registration at official site.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration can be completed at a U.S. Post Office.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "register at your local post office" (R8); "completing a form (SSS Form 1) at the post office" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration can be completed via registration forms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "download the registration form and mail it" (R8); "printable registration form" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly mentions forms for registration.

verifications.claim: Starting in 2026, many states automatically register eligible men through driver’s license or ID applications.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Currently, 46 states and territories have laws in place to automatically register eligible men when they apply for driver’s licenses or IDs" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state states already do this currently, not starting in 2026; 2026 refers to federal automatic registration.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to felony charges.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Failing to register with the Selective Service System is a felony" (R3); "Failure to register is a felony" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as felony.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to $250,000 in fines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "fine up to $250,000" (R3); "a fine of not more than $250,000" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Exact fine amount directly supported.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for federal and state-based student grants and loans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Federal student loans and grants State student aid" (R2); "State-based student loans and grant programs in 31 states" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Covers both federal and state student aid.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for federal job training and employment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Job training benefits Most federal jobs" (R2); "Federal job training under the Workforce Innovation ... Federal (and many state and local) jobs" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Directly lists federal job training and jobs.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for U.S. citizenship for immigrants.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "US citizenship for male immigrants" (R2); "denied ... US citizenship, if they are immigrants" (R3); "A delay of U.S. citizenship proceedings for immigrants" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm impact on citizenship.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to fines up to $250,000.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "fine up to $250,000" (R3); "a fine of not more than $250,000" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Exact amount and phrasing supported.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to up to five years in prison.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "five years’ imprisonment" (R3); "imprisonment for up to five years" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Precise penalty duration directly stated.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration is not a sign-up for the military.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "a man will not automatically be inducted into the military" (R1); "Registering ... does not mean you are joining the military" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly clarifies not enlistment.

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration is a list to be used if Congress and the President authorize a draft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "in case Congress and the president authorize a military draft" (R6); "list of names of men from which to draw in case of a national emergency" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly describes purpose as draft list.

verifications.claim: Registrants must notify the Selective Service of address changes until age 26.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "notify Selective Service within 10 days ... until January 1 of the year you turn 26" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Specifies notification requirement until age 26.

verifications.claim: Women are currently not required to register with the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Women are still exempt from registering" (R6); "women are still exempt" (R7); "only authorizes the registration of “male persons”" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states women not required.
